1	"""Auto-driver that advances a plan through its phases without human intervention.
2	
3	This is the mechanical loop that most orchestrators end up writing by hand:
4	read `status`, run `next_step`, repeat until terminal. All real judgment is
5	delegated to megaplan's existing phase logic — the driver only applies two
6	documented defaults:
7	
8	1. Gate ESCALATE → force-proceed (caller opts out with ``--on-escalate abort``
9	   or ``--on-escalate fail``).
10	2. Same state for N consecutive iterations → bail (stall detection).
11	
12	The driver is intentionally dumb. If a run needs judgment the driver can't
13	provide, it exits with a non-zero status and prints the state snapshot so the
14	caller can intervene.
15	"""

44	DEFAULT_MAX_CONTEXT_RETRIES = 2
45	CONTEXT_EXHAUSTION_FRAGMENT = "ran out of room in the model's context"
46	# When execute exits 0 but state.json's latest execute entry is `result=blocked`,
47	# the executor reported success-with-evidence-gaps (e.g. done tasks missing
48	# files_changed/commands_run). Retrying the same execute is structurally pointless
49	# — the model returned that shape — so we cap retries low and fail fast.
50	DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCKED_RETRIES = 1
51	# Cap on review→rework cycles before the driver bails. This mirrors the
52	# `execution.max_review_rework_cycles` config the review handler enforces
53	# internally (default 3); the auto-driver applies its own cap so that an
54	# unexpected-config or mis-routed rework loop cannot spin indefinitely.
55	DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_REWORK_CYCLES = 3

61	# remaining safe escape valve is force-proceed.

108	def _non_negative_int(value: str) -> int:
109	    try:
110	        parsed = int(value)
111	    except ValueError as error:

121	    except ValueError as error:

125	    return parsed

127	
128	def _run_megaplan(
129	    args: list[str],
130	    *,
131	    cwd: Path | None = None,
132	    timeout: float | None = None,
133	) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
134	    """Run a megaplan sub-command in its own process.
135	
136	    We shell out rather than importing the handlers directly so each phase gets
137	    a fresh argparse/handler lifecycle. This matches how external orchestrators
138	    drive the CLI and avoids subtle state leakage between phases.
139	
140	    ``timeout`` is seconds to wait before killing the subprocess. On timeout we
141	    return exit code ``PHASE_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`` and append a marker to stderr
142	    so the driver can surface it as a phase failure without crashing the loop.
143	    The subprocess is killed; any grandchildren it spawned (e.g. codex) may
144	    need a moment to settle but will exit when their parent's pipes close.
145	    """
146	    try:
147	        proc = subprocess.run(
148	            [sys.executable, "-m", "megaplan", *args],
149	            cwd=str(cwd) if cwd else None,
150	            capture_output=True,
151	            text=True,
152	            check=False,
153	            timeout=timeout,
154	        )
155	        return proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr
156	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as expired:
157	        stdout = expired.stdout if isinstance(expired.stdout, str) else ""
158	        stderr = expired.stderr if isinstance(expired.stderr, str) else ""
159	        marker = f"\n[megaplan auto] subprocess timed out after {timeout}s"
160	        return PHASE_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE, stdout, (stderr + marker).strip()
161	
162	
163	def _status(
164	    plan: str,
165	    cwd: Path | None = None,
166	    *,
167	    timeout: float = DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
168	) -> dict[str, Any]:
169	    code, out, err = _run_megaplan(["status", "--plan", plan], cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout)
170	    if code != 0:
171	        raise RuntimeError(f"megaplan status failed (exit {code}): {err.strip() or out.strip()}")
172	    return json.loads(out)

179	def _phase_command(next_step: str) -> list[str]:
180	    """Translate a `next_step` from status into the CLI args that run it.
181	
182	    Most phases are one-to-one: next_step == command. Execute adds the
183	    destructive + user-approved flags because auto-mode implies both.
184	
185	    Multi-token values like ``"override add-note"`` must be split into
186	    ``["override", "add-note"]`` so argparse sees the sub-subcommand —
187	    otherwise the whole string is passed as a single positional and
188	    argparse rejects it with `invalid choice`.
189	    """
190	    if next_step == "execute":
191	        return ["execute", "--confirm-destructive", "--user-approved"]
192	    return shlex.split(next_step)
193

195	def _resolve_plan_dir(plan: str, cwd: Path | None) -> Path | None:
196	    """Best-effort resolution of legacy or canonical orphan plan roots near ``cwd``."""
197	    return find_plan_dir(cwd or Path.cwd(), plan)

200	def _last_history_step_result(plan_dir: Path | None, step: str) -> str | None:
201	    """Return the `result` field on the most recent history entry whose step matches.
202	
203	    Used to detect when a phase completed successfully at the subprocess level
204	    but recorded `result: "blocked"` in state.json — the worker shipped output
205	    but the executor's own quality checks rejected it (e.g. done tasks missing
206	    files_changed). Returns None when state.json is missing/malformed or no
207	    matching entry exists.
208	    """
209	    if plan_dir is None:
210	        return None
211	    try:
212	        with (plan_dir / "state.json").open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
213	            state_data = json.load(handle)
214	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
215	        return None
216	    if not isinstance(state_data, dict):
217	        return None
218	    history = state_data.get("history") or []
219	    for entry in reversed(history):
220	        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("step") == step:
221	            result = entry.get("result")
222	            return result if isinstance(result, str) else None
223	    return None
224

226	def _read_execute_blocking_deviations(plan_dir: Path | None) -> list[str]:
227	    """Return the most recent execute-batch's blocking deviations (best-effort).
228	
229	    The auto-driver uses these to surface *why* execute was blocked when the
230	    final history entry's `result` is `blocked`. Reads the highest-numbered
231	    execution_batch_<n>.json and pulls the `deviations` array, filtering for
232	    the strings that build_blocking_reasons emits (advisory deviations are
233	    excluded from the surfaced reason list).
234	    """
235	    if plan_dir is None:
236	        return []
237	    try:
238	        batches = sorted(
239	            (p for p in plan_dir.iterdir() if p.name.startswith("execution_batch_") and p.suffix == ".json"),
240	            key=lambda p: p.name,
241	        )
242	    except OSError:
243	        return []
244	    if not batches:
245	        return []
246	    try:
247	        with batches[-1].open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
248	            payload = json.load(handle)
249	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
250	        return []
251	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
252	        return []
253	    deviations = payload.get("deviations") or []
254	    if not isinstance(deviations, list):
255	        return []
256	    blocking_prefixes = (
257	        "tasks have no executor update",
258	        "sense checks have no executor acknowledgment",
259	        "done tasks missing both files_changed and commands_run",
260	        "Done tasks missing sections_written",
261	    )
262	    return [
263	        str(d)
264	        for d in deviations
265	        if isinstance(d, str) and any(prefix in d for prefix in blocking_prefixes)
266	    ]
267	
268	
269	def _latest_versioned_artifact(plan_dir: Path | None, prefix: str) -> Path | None:
270	    """Return the highest-numbered versioned artifact (``<prefix>v<N>.json``)."""
271	    if plan_dir is None:
272	        return None
273	    try:
274	        candidates = [
275	            p for p in plan_dir.iterdir()
276	            if p.name.startswith(prefix) and p.suffix == ".json"
277	        ]
278	    except OSError:
279	        return None
280	    if not candidates:
281	        return None
282	
283	    def _version(path: Path) -> int:
284	        stem = path.stem  # drop .json
285	        try:
286	            return int(stem.split("v")[-1])
287	        except (ValueError, IndexError):
288	            return -1
289	
290	    candidates.sort(key=_version)
291	    return candidates[-1] if candidates else None
292

294	def _read_unresolved_flag_ids(plan_dir: Path | None) -> list[str]:
295	    """Best-effort list of unresolved flag IDs from the latest gate signals.
296	
297	    Falls back to the latest critique artifact if no gate_signals_v*.json
298	    exists yet (e.g. ESCALATE arrived from a non-gate path). Returns ``[]``
299	    on any read/parse error — callers must treat that as "no flags known"
300	    and synthesize a generic note rather than crashing.
301	    """
302	    sources = [
303	        _latest_versioned_artifact(plan_dir, "gate_signals_v"),
304	        _latest_versioned_artifact(plan_dir, "critique_v"),
305	    ]
306	    for path in sources:
307	        if path is None:
308	            continue
309	        try:
310	            with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
311	                payload = json.load(handle)
312	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
313	            continue
314	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
315	            continue
316	        # gate_signals_v*.json uses [REDACTED]; critique_v*.json
317	        # uses "flags". Either may be missing on truncated artifacts.
318	        for key in ("unresolved_flags", "flags"):
319	            flags = payload.get(key)
320	            if isinstance(flags, list) and flags:
321	                ids = [
322	                    str(f.get("id"))
323	                    for f in flags
324	                    if isinstance(f, dict) and isinstance(f.get("id"), str) and f.get("id")
325	                ]
326	                if ids:
327	                    return ids
328	    return []
329	
330	
331	def _synthesize_add_note_text(
332	    plan_dir: Path | None,
333	    *,
334	    iteration: int,
335	    attempt: int,
336	) -> str:
337	    """Build a non-empty `--note` string for an unattended add-note dispatch.
338	
339	    The orchestrator only reaches `override add-note` when the
340	    critique→revise→gate loop has failed to converge and the gate has
341	    punted to a human. Without a human, the auto-driver records why it
342	    is advancing anyway: the unresolved flag IDs (if readable) and the
343	    iteration/attempt counters so audits can spot loops.
344	    """
345	    flag_ids = _read_unresolved_flag_ids(plan_dir)
346	    if flag_ids:
347	        # Cap the inline list — strict-notes mode rejects giant blobs.
348	        head = ", ".join(flag_ids[:10])
349	        suffix = f" (+{len(flag_ids) - 10} more)" if len(flag_ids) > 10 else ""
350	        flags_part = f"; unresolved=[{head}{suffix}]"
351	    else:
352	        flags_part = "; unresolved=[unknown]"
353	    return (
354	        f"auto: critique loop unresolved at iter {iteration} "
355	        f"(add-note attempt {attempt}){flags_part}; advancing without human"
356	    )
357	
358	
359	def _build_override_add_note_command(
360	    plan: str,
361	    plan_dir: Path | None,
362	    *,
363	    iteration: int,
364	    attempt: int,
365	) -> list[str]:
366	    """Construct the full argv for ``megaplan override add-note ...``.
367	
368	    Matches the CLI contract enforced by ``cli.py::_validate_override_args``:
369	    requires both ``--plan`` and a non-empty ``--note``. Without ``--note``
370	    the subcommand fails with ``invalid_args`` and the auto-driver retries
371	    the same broken call until stall detection kills the run.
372	    """
373	    note = _synthesize_add_note_text(plan_dir, iteration=iteration, attempt=attempt)
374	    return ["override", "add-note", "--plan", plan, "--note", note]
375	
376	
377	def _sum_history_cost_usd(plan_dir: Path | None) -> float:
378	    if plan_dir is None:
379	        return 0.0
380	
381	    try:
382	        with (plan_dir / "state.json").open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
383	            state_data = json.load(handle)
384	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
385	        return 0.0
386	
387	    if not isinstance(state_data, dict):
388	        return 0.0
389	
390	    total = 0.0
391	    for entry in state_data.get("history") or []:
392	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
393	            continue
394	        try:
395	            total += float(entry.get("cost_usd", 0.0) or 0.0)
396	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
397	            continue
398	    return round(total, 6)
399	
400	
401	def _get_review_marker(plan_dir: Path | None) -> float | None:
402	    """Return a monotonically-advancing marker for the current review cycle.
403	
404	    Uses ``review.json`` mtime — each completed review phase rewrites the
405	    file, so the mtime bumps once per review cycle. This is race-free
406	    enough for stall detection: the driver only checks the marker between
407	    iterations, and mtime granularity (~1s on APFS/ext4) is finer than the
408	    minimum review runtime.
409	
410	    Returns ``None`` when no marker is available (plan dir missing, review
411	    not yet run, or stat failed) — the caller must treat ``None == None``
412	    as "no progress observed" and fall through to plain stall detection.
413	    """
414	    if plan_dir is None:
415	        return None
416	    review_path = plan_dir / "review.json"
417	    try:
418	        return review_path.stat().st_mtime
419	    except (OSError, FileNotFoundError):
420	        return None
421	
422	
423	def drive(
424	    plan: str,
425	    *,
426	    cwd: Path | None = None,
427	    stall_threshold: int = DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD,
428	    max_iterations: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS,
429	    max_review_rework_cycles: int = DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_REWORK_CYCLES,
430	    max_cost_usd: float | None = None,
431	    max_context_retries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CONTEXT_RETRIES,
432	    max_blocked_retries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCKED_RETRIES,
433	    max_add_note_attempts: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ADD_NOTE_ATTEMPTS,
434	    on_escalate: str = "force-proceed",
435	    poll_sleep: float = DEFAULT_POLL_SLEEP_SECONDS,
436	    phase_timeout: float = DEFAULT_PHASE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
437	    status_timeout: float = DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
438	    on_phase_complete: Callable[[str, int, str, str], None] | None = None,
439	    writer=sys.stdout.write,
440	) -> DriverOutcome:
441	    """Drive ``plan`` to completion.
442	
443	    Returns a DriverOutcome with a terminal status. The writer is used for
444	    human-readable progress; structured events are collected on the outcome.
445	    """
446	
447	    if on_escalate not in ESCALATE_ACTIONS:
448	        raise ValueError(f"on_escalate must be one of {ESCALATE_ACTIONS}")
449	
450	    events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
451	    last_state: str | None = None
452	    stall_count = 0
453	    last_phase: str | None = None
454	    context_retry_count = 0
455	    blocked_retry_count = 0
456	    # Consecutive `override add-note` dispatches that failed (non-zero exit).
457	    # Reset on any successful add-note OR when the next_step changes — only a
458	    # repeating add-note→fail loop should trip the escalation.
459	    add_note_failures = 0
460	
461	    # Rework-cycle tracking. When review returns `needs_rework`, the plan
462	    # ping-pongs `finalized ↔ executed ↔ finalized` while execute re-runs
463	    # batches. From the driver's naive view that looks like a stall, but
464	    # every completed review rewrites `review.json`, so its mtime is a
465	    # reliable "forward progress" marker — each advance means a real
466	    # review cycle finished since we last observed the state.
467	    plan_dir = _resolve_plan_dir(plan, cwd)
468	    last_review_marker = _get_review_marker(plan_dir)
469	    rework_cycles_observed = 0
470	
471	    def log(msg: str, **fields: Any) -> None:
472	        events.append({"msg": msg, **fields})
473	        writer(f"[auto {plan}] {msg}\n")
474	
475	    def _outcome(
476	        status: str,
477	        *,
478	        final_state: str,
479	        iterations: int,
480	        reason: str = "",
481	        last_phase: str | None = None,
482	        blocking_reasons: list[str] | None = None,
483	    ) -> DriverOutcome:
484	        return DriverOutcome(
485	            status=status,
486	            plan=plan,
487	            final_state=final_state,
488	            iterations=iterations,
489	            reason=reason,
490	            last_phase=last_phase,
491	            events=events,
492	            total_cost_usd=_sum_history_cost_usd(plan_dir),
493	            cost_cap_usd=max_cost_usd,
494	            context_retries_used=context_retry_count,
495	            max_context_retries=max_context_retries,
496	            blocked_retries_used=blocked_retry_count,
497	            max_blocked_retries=max_blocked_retries,
498	            blocking_reasons=list(blocking_reasons or []),
499	        )
500	
501	    for iteration in range(1, max_iterations + 1):
502	        try:
503	            status = _status(plan, cwd=cwd, timeout=status_timeout)
504	        except (RuntimeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
505	            log(f"status lookup failed: {error}")
506	            return _outcome(
507	                "failed",
508	                final_state=last_state or "unknown",
509	                iterations=iteration,
510	                reason=str(error),
511	                last_phase=last_phase,
512	            )
513	
514	        state = status.get("state", "")
515	
516	        if max_cost_usd is not None:
517	            cumulative = _sum_history_cost_usd(plan_dir)
518	            if cumulative > max_cost_usd:
519	                log(
520	                    f"cost cap exceeded after phase '{last_phase}': "
521	                    f"total_cost_usd={cumulative} > cost_cap_usd={max_cost_usd}",
522	                    total_cost_usd=cumulative,
523	                    cost_cap_usd=max_cost_usd,
524	                )
525	                return _outcome(
526	                    "cost_cap_exceeded",
527	                    final_state=state,
528	                    iterations=iteration,
529	                    reason=(
530	                        f"cost cap exceeded after phase '{last_phase}': "
531	                        f"{cumulative} > {max_cost_usd}"
532	                    ),
533	                    last_phase=last_phase,
534	                )
535	
536	        next_step = status.get("next_step")
537	        valid_next = status.get("valid_next") or []
538	
539	        log(
540	            f"iter {iteration} state={state} next={next_step} valid_next={valid_next}",
541	            iteration=iteration,
542	            state=state,
543	            next_step=next_step,
544	            valid_next=valid_next,
545	        )
546	
547	        # Terminal: plan reached a final state (or automation-terminal).
548	        if state in AUTOMATION_TERMINAL_STATES:
549	            if state == STATE_AWAITING_HUMAN:
550	                log("plan awaiting human verification — automation stopping")
551	                return _outcome(
552	                    "awaiting_human",
553	                    final_state=state,
554	                    iterations=iteration,
555	                    reason="plan has criteria requiring human verification",
556	                    last_phase=last_phase,
557	                )
558	            if state == STATE_TIEBREAKER_PENDING:
559	                log("tiebreaker pending — run 'megaplan tiebreaker-run --plan <name>' to execute")
560	                return _outcome(
561	                    "tiebreaker_pending",
562	                    final_state=state,
563	                    iterations=iteration,
564	                    reason="gate recommended tiebreaker — researcher/challenger run needed",
565	                    last_phase=last_phase,
566	                )
567	            if state == STATE_TIEBREAKER_READY:
568	                log("tiebreaker ready — run 'megaplan tiebreaker decide --plan <name>' to resolve")
569	                return _outcome(
570	                    "tiebreaker_ready",
571	                    final_state=state,
572	                    iterations=iteration,
573	                    reason="tiebreaker synthesis complete — awaiting human decision",
574	                    last_phase=last_phase,
575	                )
576	            log(f"terminal state reached: {state}")
577	            return _outcome(
578	                "done" if state == "done" else "aborted",
579	                final_state=state,
580	                iterations=iteration,
581	                reason=f"plan entered terminal state '{state}'",
582	                last_phase=last_phase,
583	            )
584	
585	        # Review-cycle progress: a fresh review.json means a real review
586	        # pass completed since the last iteration. This counts as forward
587	        # progress even when `state` looks unchanged (finalized→executed→
588	        # finalized during a needs_rework loop) — reset the stall counter
589	        # so execute has a full rework pass before tripping stall detection.
590	        current_review_marker = _get_review_marker(plan_dir)
591	        if (
592	            current_review_marker is not None
593	            and current_review_marker != last_review_marker
594	        ):
595	            if last_review_marker is not None:
596	                rework_cycles_observed += 1
597	                log(
598	                    f"review.json updated — rework cycle {rework_cycles_observed} "
599	                    f"observed, resetting stall counter",
600	                    rework_cycles_observed=rework_cycles_observed,
601	                )
602	                stall_count = 0
603	            last_review_marker = current_review_marker
604	
605	            if rework_cycles_observed > max_review_rework_cycles:
606	                # Review handler has its own internal cap (see
607	                # handlers.py::handle_review — force-proceeds to done when
608	                # prior_rework_count hits max_review_rework_cycles). This
609	                # driver cap is a belt-and-braces guard against config drift
610	                # or unexpected loops the handler didn't catch.
611	                log(
612	                    f"observed {rework_cycles_observed} rework cycles "
613	                    f"(cap={max_review_rework_cycles}) — bailing"
614	                )
615	                return _outcome(
616	                    "stalled",
617	                    final_state=state,
618	                    iterations=iteration,
619	                    reason=(
620	                        f"exceeded review rework cap "
621	                        f"({rework_cycles_observed} cycles > "
622	                        f"{max_review_rework_cycles}) — review keeps "
623	                        "returning needs_rework without resolving"
624	                    ),
625	                    last_phase=last_phase,
626	                )
627	
628	        # Stall detection: same state for stall_threshold+ iterations.
629	        if state == last_state:
630	            stall_count += 1
631	            if stall_count >= stall_threshold:
632	                # Distinguish an all-blocked outcome from a generic stall.
633	                # When execute reports every pending task as `blocked`, the
634	                # problem is a poisoned session or genuinely broken env —
635	                # supervisors should react differently (e.g. retry with a
636	                # fresh session) rather than just restart and loop.
637	                progress = status.get("progress") or {}
638	                tasks_blocked = int(progress.get("tasks_blocked", 0) or 0)
639	                tasks_pending = int(progress.get("tasks_pending", 0) or 0)
640	                if tasks_blocked > 0 and tasks_pending == 0:
641	                    log(
642	                        f"all pending tasks reported status=blocked "
643	                        f"({tasks_blocked} blocked) — treating as poisoned outcome"
644	                    )
645	                    return _outcome(
646	                        "blocked",
647	                        final_state=state,
648	                        iterations=iteration,
649	                        reason=(
650	                            "all tasks reported blocked — workers may be poisoned "
651	                            "or the environment may genuinely be broken"
652	                        ),
653	                        last_phase=last_phase,
654	                    )
655	                log(f"stalled at state={state} for {stall_count} iterations")
656	                return _outcome(
657	                    "stalled",
658	                    final_state=state,
659	                    iterations=iteration,
660	                    reason=(
661	                        f"stalled at '{state}' for {stall_count} iterations — "
662	                        "manual intervention required"
663	                    ),
664	                    last_phase=last_phase,
665	                )
666	        else:
667	            stall_count = 0
668	            last_state = state
669	
670	        # Escalation: no phase to run but overrides are available.
671	        if not next_step:
672	            if _has_valid_next(status, "override force-proceed"):
673	                if on_escalate == "force-proceed":
674	                    log("gate escalated — force-proceeding (per on_escalate=force-proceed)")
675	                    code, out, err = _run_megaplan(
676	                        [
677	                            "override",
678	                            "force-proceed",
679	                            "--plan",
680	                            plan,
681	                            "--reason",
682	                            "megaplan auto: escalate → force-proceed",
683	                        ],
684	                        cwd=cwd,
685	                        timeout=status_timeout,
686	                    )
687	                    if code != 0:
688	                        log(f"force-proceed failed (exit {code}): {err.strip() or out.strip()}")
689	                        # Strict-notes invariants surface as specific error
690	                        # codes — when we see them the right move is to
691	                        # surrender to the human rather than treat the
692	                        # subprocess failure as a generic auto-driver fault.
693	                        combined_text = f"{out}\n{err}"
694	                        strict_signals = (
695	                            "unabsorbed_notes_exist",
696	                            "escalate_requires_user_approval",
697	                        )
698	                        if any(signal in combined_text for signal in strict_signals):
699	                            return _outcome(
700	                                "human_required",
701	                                final_state=state,
702	                                iterations=iteration,
703	                                reason=(
704	                                    "force-proceed blocked by strict-notes — human "
705	                                    "required to address notes or approve escalate"
706	                                ),
707	                                last_phase=last_phase,
708	                            )
709	                        return _outcome(
710	                            "failed",
711	                            final_state=state,
712	                            iterations=iteration,
713	                            reason=f"override force-proceed exited {code}",
714	                            last_phase=last_phase,
715	                        )
716	                    continue
717	                if on_escalate == "abort":
718	                    log("gate escalated — aborting (per on_escalate=abort)")
719	                    _run_megaplan(
720	                        [
721	                            "override",
722	                            "abort",
723	                            "--plan",
724	                            plan,
725	                            "--reason",
726	                            "megaplan auto: escalate → abort",
727	                        ],
728	                        cwd=cwd,
729	                        timeout=status_timeout,
730	                    )
731	                    return _outcome(
732	                        "aborted",
733	                        final_state=state,
734	                        iterations=iteration,
735	                        reason="gate escalated and on_escalate=abort",
736	                        last_phase=last_phase,
737	                    )
738	                # on_escalate == "fail"
739	                log("gate escalated — failing (per on_escalate=fail)")
740	                return _outcome(
741	                    "escalated",
742	                    final_state=state,
743	                    iterations=iteration,
744	                    reason="gate escalated and on_escalate=fail — human required",
745	                    last_phase=last_phase,
746	                )
747	            log(f"no next_step and no override available (valid_next={valid_next})")
748	            return _outcome(
749	                "failed",
750	                final_state=state,
751	                iterations=iteration,
752	                reason="no next_step and no override available",
753	                last_phase=last_phase,
754	            )
755	
756	        # Run the next phase.
757	        # Special-case `override add-note`: the CLI requires a non-empty
758	        # ``--note`` argument, so we synthesize one from the latest gate
759	        # signals / critique flags. After ``max_add_note_attempts``
760	        # consecutive failed dispatches, fall through to ``override
761	        # force-proceed`` — that's the safety-net escape valve when
762	        # human intervention isn't available (Track B fallback).
763	        if next_step == "override add-note":
764	            if (
765	                max_add_note_attempts >= 0
766	                and add_note_failures >= max_add_note_attempts
767	                and _has_valid_next(status, "override force-proceed")
768	            ):
769	                log(
770	                    f"override add-note failed {add_note_failures} times — "
771	                    "escalating to override force-proceed",
772	                    add_note_failures=add_note_failures,
773	                    max_add_note_attempts=max_add_note_attempts,
774	                )
775	                cmd = [
776	                    "override",
777	                    "force-proceed",
778	                    "--plan",
779	                    plan,
780	                    "--reason",
781	                    (
782	                        f"megaplan auto: {add_note_failures} add-note retries "
783	                        "failed, forcing proceed"
784	                    ),
785	                ]
786	                last_phase = "override force-proceed"
787	                add_note_failures = 0
788	            else:
789	                cmd = _build_override_add_note_command(
790	                    plan,
791	                    plan_dir,
792	                    iteration=iteration,
793	                    attempt=add_note_failures + 1,
794	                )
795	                last_phase = next_step
796	        else:
797	            # Any non-add-note dispatch resets the add-note failure counter —
798	            # only a repeating add-note→fail loop should trigger escalation.
799	            add_note_failures = 0
800	            cmd = _phase_command(next_step) + ["--plan", plan]
801	            last_phase = next_step
802	        log(f"running: megaplan {' '.join(cmd)}", phase=next_step, timeout=phase_timeout)
803	        code, out, err = _run_megaplan(cmd, cwd=cwd, timeout=phase_timeout)
804	        if next_step == "override add-note" and last_phase == "override add-note":
805	            if code != 0:
806	                add_note_failures += 1
807	            else:
808	                add_note_failures = 0
809	        if max_context_retries > 0:
810	            while (
811	                next_step == "execute"
812	                and code != 0
813	                and CONTEXT_EXHAUSTION_FRAGMENT.lower() in ((out or "") + (err or "")).lower()
814	            ):
815	                if context_retry_count >= max_context_retries:
816	                    log(
817	                        f"context exhaustion retry cap reached ({max_context_retries}) — bailing",
818	                        context_retries_used=context_retry_count,
819	                        max_context_retries=max_context_retries,
820	                    )
821	                    return _outcome(
822	                        "context_retry_exhausted",
823	                        final_state=state,
824	                        iterations=iteration,
825	                        reason=(
826	                            f"context exhaustion retry cap reached "
827	                            f"({context_retry_count}/{max_context_retries})"
828	                        ),
829	                        last_phase=last_phase,
830	                    )
831	                log(
832	                    "context exhaustion detected — retrying execute with "
833	                    f"--fresh (retry {context_retry_count + 1}/{max_context_retries})",
834	                    context_retries_used=context_retry_count,
835	                    max_context_retries=max_context_retries,
836	                    next_context_retry=context_retry_count + 1,
837	                )
838	                context_retry_count += 1
839	                if "--fresh" not in cmd:
840	                    cmd = [*cmd, "--fresh"]
841	                code, out, err = _run_megaplan(cmd, cwd=cwd, timeout=phase_timeout)
842	        if code == PHASE_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE:
843	            log(f"phase '{next_step}' timed out after {phase_timeout}s — stall detection will enforce the cap")
844	        elif code != 0:
845	            # Don't bail immediately — megaplan often records a partial failure
846	            # in state.json and the next status() reveals a recoverable valid_next.
847	            # Stall detection will still kill infinite loops.
848	            log(f"phase '{next_step}' exited {code}: {err.strip() or out.strip()[-400:]}")
849	
850	        if on_phase_complete and next_step in {"plan", "critique", "gate", "finalize", "execute", "review"}:
851	            try:
852	                on_phase_complete(next_step, int(code or 0), out, err)
853	            except Exception as error:  # pragma: no cover - defensive callback boundary
854	                log(f"phase-complete callback failed after '{next_step}': {error}")
855	                return _outcome(
856	                    "failed",
857	                    final_state=state,
858	                    iterations=iteration,
859	                    reason=f"phase-complete callback failed after '{next_step}': {error}",
860	                    last_phase=last_phase,
861	                )
862	
863	        # Worker-blocked detection: execute exited 0 (or returned partial work)
864	        # but state.json's latest execute history entry has `result: "blocked"`.
865	        # Without this guard the driver would re-run execute every iteration
866	        # (state stays `finalized`) until stall-threshold finally kills it —
867	        # which we observed in IRL bake-offs with hermes-based executors.
868	        if next_step == "execute" and code in (0, None) and max_blocked_retries >= 0:
869	            execute_result = _last_history_step_result(plan_dir, "execute")
870	            if execute_result == "blocked":
871	                deviations = _read_execute_blocking_deviations(plan_dir)
872	                if blocked_retry_count >= max_blocked_retries:
873	                    log(
874	                        f"execute blocked by quality gates and retry cap reached "
875	                        f"({max_blocked_retries}) — bailing",
876	                        blocked_retries_used=blocked_retry_count,
877	                        max_blocked_retries=max_blocked_retries,
878	                        blocking_reasons=deviations,
879	                    )
880	                    return _outcome(
881	                        "worker_blocked",
882	                        final_state=state,
883	                        iterations=iteration,
884	                        reason=(
885	                            "execute returned result=blocked from quality gates "
886	                            f"after {blocked_retry_count + 1} attempt(s); "
887	                            f"retry cap {max_blocked_retries} reached"
888	                        ),
889	                        last_phase=last_phase,
890	                        blocking_reasons=deviations,
891	                    )
892	                blocked_retry_count += 1
893	                log(
894	                    f"execute blocked by quality gates — retrying "
895	                    f"({blocked_retry_count}/{max_blocked_retries})",
896	                    blocked_retries_used=blocked_retry_count,
897	                    max_blocked_retries=max_blocked_retries,
898	                    blocking_reasons=deviations,
899	                )
900	
901	        if poll_sleep > 0:
902	            time.sleep(poll_sleep)
903	
904	    # Hit iteration cap.
905	    log(f"hit max_iterations={max_iterations}")
906	    return _outcome(
907	        "cap",
908	        final_state=last_state or "unknown",

1037	def _atomic_write_text(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
1038	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1039	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
1040	        "w",
1041	        encoding="utf-8",
1042	        dir=path.parent,
1043	        prefix=f".{path.name}.",
1044	        suffix=".tmp",
1045	        delete=False,
1046	    ) as handle:
1047	        tmp_path = Path(handle.name)
1048	        handle.write(text)
1049	        handle.flush()
1050	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1051	    os.replace(tmp_path, path)
1052	
1053	
1054	def run_auto(root: Path, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
1055	    """CLI entry point. Returns a POSIX exit code suitable for ``sys.exit``."""
1056	    outcome = drive(
1057	        args.plan,
1058	        cwd=root,
1059	        stall_threshold=args.stall_threshold,
1060	        max_iterations=args.max_iterations,
1061	        max_review_rework_cycles=args.max_review_rework_cycles,
1062	        max_cost_usd=args.max_cost_usd,
1063	        max_context_retries=args.max_context_retries,
1064	        max_blocked_retries=args.max_blocked_retries,
1065	        max_add_note_attempts=args.max_add_note_attempts,
1066	        on_escalate=args.on_escalate,
1067	        poll_sleep=args.poll_sleep,
1068	        phase_timeout=args.phase_timeout,
1069	        status_timeout=args.status_timeout,
1070	    )
1071	    outcome_json = outcome.to_json()
1072	    if args.outcome_file:
1073	        _atomic_write_text(Path(args.outcome_file), outcome_json)
1074	    sys.stdout.write(outcome_json + "\n")
1075	    # Exit codes: 0 done/aborted, 1 failed/unknown, 2 stalled, 3 escalated,
1076	    # 4 iteration cap, 5 blocked, 6 cost cap exceeded, 7 context retry exhausted,
1077	    # 8 worker_blocked.
1078	    if outcome.status == "done":
1079	        return 0
1080	    if outcome.status == "aborted":
1081	        return 0  # user-requested abort is not a failure
1082	    if outcome.status == "stalled":
1083	        return 2
1084	    if outcome.status == "escalated":
1085	        return 3
1086	    if outcome.status == "cap":
1087	        return 4
1088	    if outcome.status == "blocked":
1089	        return 5
1090	    if outcome.status == "cost_cap_exceeded":
1091	        return 6
1092	    if outcome.status == "context_retry_exhausted":
1093	        return 7
1094	    if outcome.status == "worker_blocked":
1095	        return 8
1096	    return 1
1097

228	def _merge_gate_worker_attempt(base: WorkerResult, retry: WorkerResult) -> WorkerResult:
229	    base.payload = retry.payload
230	    base.raw_output = "\n\n".join(part for part in [base.raw_output, retry.raw_output] if part)
231	    if base.trace_output or retry.trace_output:
232	        base.trace_output = "\n\n".join(part for part in [base.trace_output, retry.trace_output] if part)
233	    base.duration_ms += retry.duration_ms
234	    base.cost_usd += retry.cost_usd
235	    base.session_id = retry.session_id or base.session_id
236	    base.prompt_tokens += retry.prompt_tokens
237	    base.completion_tokens += retry.completion_tokens
238	    base.total_tokens += retry.total_tokens
239	    return base

241	def _merge_resolution_tradeoffs_into_payload(gate_summary: dict[str, Any], worker_payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
242	    raw_tradeoffs = worker_payload.get("accepted_tradeoffs", [])
243	    merged_tradeoffs = list(raw_tradeoffs) if isinstance(raw_tradeoffs, list) else []
244	    existing_ids = {
245	        item.get("flag_id")
246	        for item in merged_tradeoffs
247	        if isinstance(item, dict) and isinstance(item.get("flag_id"), str)
248	    }
249	    unresolved_by_id = {
250	        flag.get("id"): flag
251	        for flag in gate_summary.get("unresolved_flags", [])
252	        if isinstance(flag, dict) and isinstance(flag.get("id"), str)
253	    }
254	    for resolution in gate_summary.get("flag_resolutions", []):
255	        if not isinstance(resolution, dict) or resolution.get("action") != "accept_tradeoff":
256	            continue
257	        flag_id = resolution.get("flag_id")
258	        if not isinstance(flag_id, str) or flag_id in existing_ids:
259	            continue
260	        flag = unresolved_by_id.get(flag_id)
261	        if not isinstance(flag, dict):
262	            continue
263	        concern = flag.get("concern")
264	        if not isinstance(concern, str):
265	            continue
266	        tradeoff = {"flag_id": flag_id, "concern": concern}
267	        subsystem = flag.get("subsystem")
268	        if isinstance(subsystem, str) and subsystem.strip():
269	            tradeoff["subsystem"] = subsystem
270	        merged_tradeoffs.append(tradeoff)
271	        existing_ids.add(flag_id)
272	    worker_payload["accepted_tradeoffs"] = merged_tradeoffs

# Megaplan critique-loop runaway investigation

## 1. Existing iteration limits

All caps live in the **auto-driver** (`megaplan/auto.py`); none in the gate/critique/revise handlers:

- `DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD = 5` — same `state` value for 5 consecutive iterations bails (auto.py:39, 628-665). **Crucially, the critique→revise→gate loop transitions `critiqued → critiqued` (revise leaves state intact, gate sets it back to `STATE_CRITIQUED` at gate.py:213) so each cycle changes `state` and the stall counter resets to 0** (auto.py:666-668).
- `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 200` (auto.py:40, 501) — hard outer loop cap; nowhere near tripped.
- `DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_REWORK_CYCLES = 3` (auto.py:55, 605-626) — applies to *review→rework*, not critique→revise.
- `DEFAULT_MAX_ADD_NOTE_ATTEMPTS = 2` (auto.py:62, 763-787) — only fires after the gate recommends ESCALATE *and* add-note fails twice. In a converging-then-stuck loop where the gate keeps recommending ITERATE, this never triggers.
- No critique-iteration cap in `handlers/critique.py`, `handlers/gate.py`, or `evaluation.py`. `iteration_pressure.py:111` *measures* recurring flags but only emits guidance text (evaluation.py:821-825), never forces termination.

## 2. Why the loop ran (rerun2 = 6 critique iterations, ~22+ harness iters)

Plan dir: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/.megaplan-worktrees/phase-9-dcccr-loweff-rerun2-20260505/deepseek-claude-critique-cr-low/.megaplan/plans/phase-9-dcccr-loweff-rerun2-20260505/`

- `state.json`: 22 history entries; `iteration=6`; `current_state=critiqued`; `last_gate.recommendation=ESCALATE`.
- `meta.weighted_scores = [27, 31.5, 29.5, 30, 30, 49]` — plateau at 30 for v3-v5 then jumped.
- `unresolved_flags` ids across `gate_signals_v1..v6.json` strictly **accumulate** (v6 carries every prior flag id plus new ones: 28 total). The flag-registry is never pruning resolved flags between iterations — the same `correctness-1`, `scope-1`, `callers-1`, etc. are present in v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, v6. The critic kept emitting net-new flag IDs (FLAG-CR-007/008/009 then 012/014/015 then 016/017/018) on top of the persistent generic ones.
- Each critique→gate cycle: gate returns ITERATE (rec gate.py:218-219 → next_step="revise"), revise runs, critique runs, gate runs again. State oscillates but never stalls because `_apply_gate_outcome` toggles state.
- 3 of 5 revises came back as `result=error` (state.json history) — failed revise that nonetheless resulted in a fresh `critique` next round, perpetuating the loop.

So: **the loop didn't hit any cap because no cap exists for this exact path**. Stall detection can't fire (state changes every iteration), max_iterations=200 is too generous, and review-rework / add-note caps don't apply until either review or ESCALATE.

## 3. The gap

Megaplan has **no governor on the plan-phase critique-revise loop**. The gate's `build_orchestrator_guidance` (evaluation.py:821-825) detects "score plateaued + recurring critiques" and *advises* force-proceed — but this is text in `orchestrator_guidance`, never wired to a hard limit or a `next_step` change. The gate keeps emitting `recommendation=ITERATE` while a human reads the prose hint. In auto-mode there is no human, and the driver doesn't read `orchestrator_guidance`.

## 4. Recommendations (no code change yet)

1. **Add a hard critique-iteration cap in the gate handler.** In `megaplan/handlers/gate.py` `_apply_gate_outcome` (~line 218), when `recommendation == "ITERATE"` and `state["iteration"] >= cap`, downgrade to ESCALATE with rationale "critique loop exceeded N iterations". Robustness-tier-aware: `light=4`, `standard=6`, `robust=10`. Mirrors the existing review rework pattern.

2. **Convergence-failure detection in the gate.** Same location, gate.py:218: when the latest `gate_signals_v*.json` flag-ID set ⊇ the previous iteration's set (no flags resolved between iterations) for 2 consecutive iterations, downgrade ITERATE → ESCALATE. The data is already computed in `iteration_pressure.compute_iteration_pressure` (iteration_pressure.py:111); just need to act on it.

3. **Mirror auto-driver guard.** In `auto.py:drive` (~line 501, alongside `rework_cycles_observed`), add a `critique_iterations_observed` counter incremented when `last_phase == "critique"` with a default cap (e.g. 6) and a `--max-critique-iterations` CLI flag (auto.py:933 area). Belt-and-braces if the handler-level cap is misconfigured.

Net: rec #1 is the cheap, correct fix (handler-side). Rec #3 is the defensive complement.

A **dual-path** strategy preserves backward compatibility: when a compiled plan exists at `<pack>/build/<name>.json`, the runtime-replay path runs; when it doesn't, the Phase 5 scaffold file-diff path (pre-existing captured `events.jsonl` in `<pack>/fixtures/<name>/`) runs unchanged.\n\n**Key decisions verified against source (this revision):**\n- **CodeStep.command is a `str` not `argv`** — source: `plan.py:58-63` shows `command: str`. The runner uses `shlex.split(step.command)` for subprocess invocation. (Addresses `correctness-1`)\n- **Runner drives code steps through `gate_command` → subprocess → `record_dispatch_complete`** — The production flow at `gate.py:510-604` (`gate_command`) calls `_dispatch_code` (line 573-586) which emits `step_dispatched` (line 847) and applies task-run env vars (line 848). The runner MUST invoke `gate_command` to get the `GateDecision`, then `subprocess.run(shlex.split(decision produces no command tokens — the command is on the step))`, then `record_dispatch_complete(decision, returncode)`. **No bypassing `gate_command`.** (Addresses `correctness-2`, `FLAG-CR-012`)\n- **Attested-step auto-approval reuses the `_ack_approve` pattern** — Source: `lifecycle_ack.py:190-228` constructs incoming command as `step.command + \" --agent author_test\"` (or `--actor author_test`), calls `gate_command(slug, incoming, [], root=projects_root)`, then `record_dispatch_complete(decision, 0)`. The runner mirrors this exactly. `match_attested_command` (`gate.py:1025-1061`) strips `--agent`/`--actor` tokens and compares the remainder to `step.command` — proven to work. (Addresses `callers`, `FLAG-CR-015`)\n- **`builtin/hype.py` alongside `builtin/hype/` loads correctly** — `_load_module_isolated` (`compile.py:52-69`) uses `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` with a unique synthetic module name, bypassing Python's normal import resolution. `builtin/hype.py` loads without collision with the folder package. (Addresses `scope`, `issue_hints`)\n- **`build/` is gitignored** — `.gitignore` line 60: `artagents/packs/*/build/`. The compiled `build/hype.json` must be regenerated on a fresh checkout. The plan documents `author compile builtin.hype` as a prerequisite and the runner/tests compile on-the-fly. Golden files live under `golden/` (not gitignored) and will be committed. The Phase 5 scaffold path (file-diff of pre-written captured files at `fixtures/<name>/events.jsonl`) is retained as a backward-compatible fallback when no compiled plan exists at `<pack>/build/<name>.json`.\n\n**Source-verified decisions from this revision**:\n- `CodeStep.command` is a `str` (core/task/plan.py:60) — the runner must use `shlex.split(step.command)` for subprocess argv, never reference `.command_tokens` which does not exist.\n- `_dispatch_code` (gate.py:790-860) emits `step_dispatched` (line 847), applies `ARTAGENTS_TASK_*` env vars (line 848), and handles reentry detection (lines 807-845). The runner MUST go through `gate_command` before running the subprocess — bypassing it loses `step_dispatched` emission, `apply_task_run_env`, and reentry semantics.\n- `cmd_ack._ack_approve` (lifecycle_ack.py:205-214) constructs the incoming command as `peek.step.command` + `--agent <id>` (or `--actor`). `match_attested_command` (gate.py:1025-1061) strips identity tokens and compares the remainder to `step.command`. The flow is correct for programmatic invocation with `--agent author_test`.\n- `artagents/packs/*/build/` is gitignored (.gitignore:60). The compiled `build/hype.json` must be regenerated on fresh checkout via `artagents author compile builtin.hype`.\n- **REPO STATE VERIFIED (Revision 5): No `artagents/packs/builtin/hype/` directory or `builtin/hype.py` file exists.** A previous gate critique claimed this folder exists — it does not. `search_files` with patterns `*hype*` and `**/hype/*` under `artagents/packs/` return zero matches. The only hype-named files in the repo are `examples/hype.*.json` output artifacts and `tests/test_hype_cut_invariants.py` — neither is a pack directory. The DSL smoke orchestrator `artagents/packs/builtin/hype.py` can be created cleanly without collision.\n- `child_subprocess_env` (env.py:68-81) does not currently propagate `ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST`. Must add it to the key list.\n- `step_dir_for_path` (plan.py:115-142) resolves to `<project>/runs/<run_id>/steps/<path_segments>/...`. The runner MUST set `cwd=step_dir_for_path(...)` for subprocess invocations so that produces files land where `_run_inline_checks` looks for them — NOT `cwd=run_dir` or `cwd=fixture_inputs`.\n\n## Phase 1: Foundation — Normalization + Auto-Approval\n\n### Step 1: Create `artagents/core/task/normalize.py` — event normalization\n**Scope:** Small, new file (~120 lines)\n\n1. **Implement** `normalize_event(event: dict, run_dir: Path) -> dict`:\n   - Strip volatile fields: `ts`, `hash`, `run_id`, `pid`.\n   - Replace absolute paths anchored at `run_dir` with `<RUN_DIR>/<rel>`. For any string value that starts with `str(run_dir)`, replace the prefix. Also replace `str(run_dir.parent)` (the project root) with `<PROJECT_DIR>`.\n   - Keep all structural fields: `kind`, `plan_step_id`, `plan_step_path`, `command`, `returncode`, `attestor_kind`, `attestor_id`, `evidence`, `check_id`, `produces_name`, `cas_sha256`, `iteration`, `item_id`, `reason`, `on_exhaust`, `max_iterations`, `child_plan_hash`, `actor`, `plan_hash`, `item_ids`, `source`, `path_tuple`.\n\n2. **Implement** `normalize_events_jsonl(path: Path, run_dir: Path) -> list[dict]`:\n   - Read lines, JSON-decode each, pass through `normalize_event`, return list.\n\n3. **Implement** `normalize_line(line: str, run_dir: Path) -> str`:\n   - Thin wrapper that JSON-decodes, normalizes, re-encodes with `sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False`. Returns raw line on decode failure (so malformed lines surface in diff).\n\n4. **Document**: Hash-chain hashes (`hash` field) are stripped (not recomputed) because they depend on `ts` which is volatile. Structural fields alone are sufficient for diffing event drift. `ts` is stripped because it's a UTC timestamp that varies per run. `run_id` is stripped because the runner generates a fresh one each time. These strips are a **superset** of `_strip_volatile`'s `(ts, hash)` — scaffold fixtures that include `run_id` in their pre-written JSON will see it stripped from both golden and captured sides equally, so the diff outcome is unchanged.\n\n### Step 2: Add auto-approval bypass to `validate_attested_identity` in `artagents/core/task/gate.py`\n**Scope:** Tiny, modify existing function (~6 lines)\n\n1. **Add early return** at line 1074 of gate.py (right after the mutually-exclusive `--agent`/`--actor` check, before the `step.ack.kind` branch at line 1075):\n   ```python\n   # Auto-approval for author test: requires BOTH env var AND synthetic identity.\n   if os.environ.get(\"ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST\") == \"1\":\n       if args.agent == \"author_test\" or args.actor == \"author_test\":\n           kind = \"agent\" if args.agent == \"author_test\" else \"actor\"\n           return kind, \"author_test\"\n   ```\n   This double-gates auto-approval on both the env var AND the synthetic identity `author_test`, so accidental `ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST=1` leakage from a parent shell cannot bypass identity validation unless the command also carries the `author_test` identity. The `task_actor_env() != args.actor` check at line 1082 is never reached for actor-ack steps under this bypass, so `ARTAGENTS_ACTOR` does not need to be set.\n\n2. **Propagate env to children**: In `artagents/core/task/env.py`, add `\"ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST\"` to the key list in `child_subprocess_env` (line 71-77) alongside `TASK_RUN_ID_ENV` et al. so code-step subprocesses that may dispatch nested attested sub-steps inherit the auto-approval env.\n\n## Phase 2: Runtime Replay Engine\n\n### Step 3: Create `artagents/orchestrate/author_test_runner.py` — runtime replay\n**Scope:** Medium, new file (~230 lines)\n\n1. **Implement** `run_plan_in_scratch(plan_json: dict, fixture_dir: Path, pack: str, name: str, packs_root: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]`:\n   - Returns `(events_jsonl_path, run_dir)`.\n   - Create temp directory via `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=\"author_test_\")` as the scratch root.\n   - Inside the scratch root, create `<scratch>/packs/<pack>/build/` directory and write the compiled `plan_json` to `<scratch>/packs/<pack>/build/<name>.json`.\n   - Use project slug `author_test_smoke` (validated per `validate_project_slug`).\n   - **Env safety**: Save original `ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST` (and `ARTAGENTS_FIXTURE_DIR`). Set `ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST=1` in `os.environ`. Restore in `finally`.\n   - **Call `cmd_start`** (imported from `artagents.core.task.lifecycle`):\n     ```python\n     from artagents.core.task.lifecycle import cmd_start\n     rc = cmd_start([f\"{pack}.{name}\", \"--project\", slug], packs_root=scratch_packs, projects_root=scratch_projects)\n     if rc != 0:\n         raise RuntimeError(f\"cmd_start returned {rc}\")\n     ```\n     `cmd_start` (lifecycle.py:130-220) reads the compiled plan from `<packs_root>/<pack>/build/<name>.json` (line 162), writes it to `<project>/plan.json` (line 179), creates run dir (line 198-199), writes `active_run.json` (line 201), and appends `run_started` event (line 205). The runner does NOT pre-write plan.json — `cmd_start` handles it entirely.\n\n2. **Copy fixtures**: After `cmd_start` succeeds, read `active_run.json` from `<project>` to get `run_id`, compute `run_dir = project_dir / \"runs\" / run_id`, copy `fixture_dir/*` to `run_dir / \"fixture_inputs\" /`, set `os.environ[\"ARTAGENTS_FIXTURE_DIR\"] = str(run_dir / \"fixture_inputs\")`.\n\n3. **Drive the plan loop** using `peek_current_step` + `gate_command` + `cmd_ack`:\n   - Loop variables: `proj_root = project_dir(slug, root=scratch_projects)`, `plan = load_plan(proj_root / \"plan.json\")`, `events_path = proj_root / \"runs\" / run_id / \"events.jsonl\"`.\n   - Loop:\n     a. Reload `plan` and `events` from disk (events grow as steps complete).\n     b. Call `peek = peek_current_step(plan, events, slug, project_root=proj_root, run_id=run_id)` (gate.py:454-507).\n     c. If `peek.exhausted` or `peek.step is None` → break.\n     d. **If `isinstance(peek.step, CodeStep)`** (plan.py:58-63, `command` is a `str`):\n        - Call `gate_command` with `command=peek.step.command` to emit `step_dispatched` and apply `ARTAGENTS_TASK_*` env vars:\n          ```python\n          decision = gate_command(slug, peek.step.command, [], root=scratch_projects)\n          ```\n          `gate_command` (gate.py:510-604) auto-traverses to the leaf, dispatches via `_dispatch_code` (line 574), which emits `step_dispatched` (line 847) and calls `apply_task_run_env` (line 848).\n        - Compute `cwd = step_dir_for_path(slug, run_id, peek.path_tuple, iteration=peek.iteration, item_id=peek.item_id, root=scratch_projects)`. Create the directory if it doesn't exist.\n        - Run the subprocess using `shlex.split(peek.step.command)` (because `step.command` is a `str`, not a list — plan.py:60):\n          ```python\n          cmd_tokens = shlex.split(peek.step.command)\n          proc = subprocess.run(cmd_tokens, cwd=cwd, env=child_subprocess_env(), capture_output=True)\n          ```\n        - `cwd` is `step_dir_for_path(...)` so produces files written by the step land where `_run_inline_checks` expects them.\n        - Call `record_dispatch_complete(decision, proc.returncode)` (gate.py:1096-1107) which emits `step_completed` (line 1104) and runs inline produces checks (line 1106-1107).\n     e. **If `isinstance(peek.step, AttestedStep)`** (plan.py:67-74):\n        - Build ack args based on `peek.step.ack.kind`:\n          - If `\"agent\"`: `ack_argv = [STEP_PATH_SEP.join(peek.path_tuple), \"--project\", slug, \"--decision\", \"approve\", \"--agent\", \"author_test\"]`\n          - If `\"actor\"`: `ack_argv = [..., \"--actor\", \"author_test\"]`\n        - Include `--item <peek.item_id>` if `peek.item_id` is set.\n        - Call `cmd_ack(ack_argv, projects_root=scratch_projects)` (lifecycle_ack.py:102-187).\n          `cmd_ack` calls `peek_current_step` to verify cursor (line 158-173), then `_ack_approve` (line 190-228) which constructs the incoming command as `peek.step.command + \" --agent author_test\"` (line 205-214), calls `gate_command` (line 217), which routes to `_dispatch_attested` (gate.py:904-973), which calls `match_attested_command` (line 918) and `validate_attested_identity` (line 922). The auto-approval bypass in Step 2 short-circuits identity validation and returns `(\"agent\", \"author_test\")`. Then `_dispatch_attested` emits `step_attested` (line 941-943) and runs inline checks.\n     f. After each loop iteration, the events file has grown — next iteration's `peek_current_step` will see the new events.\n\n4. **Cleanup**: Use `try/finally`:\n   - Restore `ARTAGENTS_AUTHOR_TEST` to original value (or `pop` if not originally set).\n   - Restore `ARTAGENTS_FIXTURE_DIR` to original value.\n   - If `ARTAGENTS_KEEP_SCRATCH=1` is set, print the scratch path and skip deletion; otherwise `shutil.rmtree` the temp directory.\n\n5. **Edge cases**:\n   - If the plan has no steps, `peek_current_step` returns exhausted immediately (gate.py:475-476).\n   - Code step subprocess failure: nonzero returncode is recorded in `step_completed` but does not halt the run. `peek_current_step` advances the cursor past it.\n   - `cmd_start` might fail if `active_run.json` already exists for the slug. The scratch dir is fresh, so this won't happen. If the slug is reused across calls, `shutil.rmtree` the project dir before `cmd_start`.\n   - `step_dir_for_path` is the canonical path resolver for produces checks — the runner must use it for `cwd` so that produce files land in the correct step directory.\n\n## Phase 3: Wire `author test` CLI\n\n### Step 4: Rewrite `_cmd_test` and update parser in `artagents/orchestrate/cli.py`\n**Scope:** Medium, replace Phase 5 scaffold logic with dual-path (~130 lines changed/added)\n\n1. **Parser change** (`_build_parser`, line 462-471):\n   - Keep the existing `test_p.add_argument(\"qualified_id\", ...)` for backward compat (scaffold tests pass `[\"test\", \"demo.app\", \"--fixture\", \"f1\"]`).\n   - Add optional flags:\n     ```python\n     test_p.add_argument(\"--pack\", default=None, help=\"pack name (e.g. 'builtin')\")\n     test_p.add_argument(\"--orchestrator\", default=None, help=\"orchestrator name (e.g. 'hype')\")\n     ```\n     The `qualified_id` positional remains required in argparse (for backward compat), but in dispatch we resolve the effective qid from either form.\n   - Keep `test_p.add_argument(\"--fixture\", required=True, ...)`.\n   - Add `test_p.add_argument(\"--regenerate\", action=\"store_true\", ...)`.\n\n2. **Dispatch** (in `main`, line 491-492):\n   - If `args.pack` and `args.orchestrator` are both set: use `qid = f\"{args.pack}.{args.orchestrator}\"` as the effective qualified id.\n   - Otherwise: use `args.qualified_id` (the positional).\n   - Call `_cmd_test(qid, args.fixture, args.regenerate, packs_root)`.\n\n3. **New `_cmd_test` signature and body**:\n   ```python\n   def _cmd_test(qid: str, fixture_name: str, regenerate: bool, packs_root: Optional[Path]) -> int\n   ```\n   - Resolve `root = _packs_root_arg(packs_root)`, `pack, name = _qualified_split(qid)`, `pack_root = root / pack`.\n   - Check for compiled plan at `<pack_root>/build/<name>.json`.\n   - **Path A: Runtime replay** (compiled plan exists):\n     a. Load `plan_json = json.loads(build_path.read_text())`.\n     b. Load fixture dir at `<pack_root>/fixtures/<fixture_name>/` (must exist, return 2 if missing).\n     c. Call `run_plan_in_scratch(plan_json, fixture_dir, pack, name, root)` → `(events_path, run_dir)`.\n     d. Normalize captured events: `captured = normalize_events_jsonl(events_path, run_dir)`.\n     e. Golden path: `<pack_root>/golden/<fixture_name>.events.jsonl`.\n     f. If `--regenerate`:\n        - Write `captured` as normalized JSON lines to golden path (one JSON object per line, `json.dumps` with `sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False`).\n        - Print: \"regenerated golden at <golden_path> — commit this file if the change is intentional\".\n        - Return 0.\n     g. If golden missing/empty AND not `--regenerate`:\n        - Print: \"no golden at <golden_path>; run with --regenerate to capture the first golden\".\n        - Return 2.\n     h. Otherwise: load golden, normalize each line (using the same `run_dir` for path replacement), diff with `difflib.unified_diff`. Return 0 on match, 1 on drift.\n   - **Path B: Phase 5 scaffold fallback** (no compiled plan):\n     - This path is reached when `<pack_root>/build/<name>.json` does not exist.\n     - Golden path: `<pack_root>/golden/<fixture_name>.events.jsonl`.\n     - Captured: `<pack_root>/fixtures/<fixture_name>/events.jsonl`.\n     - Check golden exists and non-empty — if not, print Phase 9 message and return 2.\n     - Check captured exists — if not, print message and return 2.\n     - Diff using `normalize_line` (from normalize.py, not `_strip_volatile`). Return 0/1.\n\n4. **Remove `_strip_volatile`**: Delete the function and `_VOLATILE_EVENT_FIELDS` constant (~lines 287-308). Import `normalize_line` from `normalize.py` instead. Update the Path B fallback code (lines 357-358) to use `normalize_line(line, Path(\".\"))` — since scaffold fixtures don't contain absolute paths, `run_dir=Path(\".\")` is harmless (no string will match `\".\"` as an absolute path prefix).\n\n## Phase 4: Golden Fixture for Smoke Test\n\n### Step 5: Create `artagents/packs/builtin/hype.py` — DSL smoke orchestrator\n**Scope:** Small, new file (~25 lines)\n\n1. **Implement** a minimal DSL orchestrator in the `builtin` pack:\n   ```python\n   \"\"\"Smoke-test orchestrator for Phase 9 golden runs.\n\n   Reads input from ARTAGENTS_FIXTURE_DIR (set by author test runner) and\n   writes a produces file to CWD. The runner sets cwd=step_dir_for_path(...)\n   so the file lands where the inline file_nonempty check expects it.\n   \"\"\"\n   import json\n   import os\n   import sys\n   from artagents.orchestrate import orchestrator, code, file_nonempty\n\n   @orchestrator(\"builtin.hype\")\n   def hype():\n       return [\n           code(\n               \"smoke_step\",\n               argv=[sys.executable, \"-c\",\n                     \"import json, os; \"\n                     \"fixture_dir = os.environ.get('ARTAGENTS_FIXTURE_DIR', '.'); \"\n                     \"# Write produces artifact to CWD (which the runner sets to step_dir_for_path)\\n\"\n                     \"json.dump({'ok': True, 'fixture_dir': fixture_dir}, open('out.json', 'w'))\"],\n               produces={\"out\": file_nonempty()},\n           ),\n       ]\n   ```\n   The `code()` DSL function accepts `argv` as a list — this becomes `step.command` as a shell-quoted string in the compiled plan. # Root cause: a hybrid of **(B) + (E)**, not (A) or (D)

**Statement:** Revise generally addressed flagged issues each cycle (addressed-rate climbed from 0/15 → 25/3), but the critic kept finding *new, real defects on different surface area* every iteration — and at iter 6 the revise model itself degraded into hallucination, inventing fictional "repo state" claims (a missing folder that exists; phantom code corruption to repair) that the critic correctly verified and flagged. The handler's `MAX_ITERATIONS=6` cap is what finally surfaced it as `ESCALATE`. Revise errors did happen (3 of 5 cycles had a first-attempt failure) but the harness retry-recovered each time, so (D) is not the mechanism — the real story is (B) unbounded critic surface + (E) revise quality regression at v6.

## Per-iteration ledger

| iter | gate score (lower=better) | flags raised | new flag IDs | persistent | unresolved addressed/open | revise result | plan delta (words) |
|------|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | 27   | 5 | CR-001..005 | — | 0 / 15 | (plan, no revise) | 1131 (baseline) |
| 2 | 31.5 | 6 | CR-006..010 | CR-002 | 6 / 12 | success | +586 (1131→1717) |
| 3 | 29.5 | 5 | CR-011..015 | none | 9 / 9  | success | +326 (1717→2043) |
| 4 | 30   | 3 | CR-016, CR-017 | CR-013 | 11 / 7 | error then retry-success ("Plan must include at least one step section") | +355 (2043→2398) |
| 5 | 30   | 2 | CR-018, CR-019 | none | 14 / 4 | error then retry-success (same structural validation) | +217 (2398→2615) |
| 6 | **49** (worst) | 2 | CR-020, CR-021 | none | 25 / 3 | Hermes JSON parse failure ("could not extract JSON from response (24 chars)") then retry-success | **−1449** (2615→**1166**, plan halved) |

Iter-1 critic raised 5 ID'd flags (`FLAG-CR-*`) but gate's own checklist contributed 10 more synthetic flags (`issue_hints-1`, `correctness-1..3`, `scope-1..2`, `all_locations-1..2`, `callers-1..2`) — that's the "15 unresolved" inflation. Subsequent cycles inherit and steadily resolve those.

## Evidence

1. **Critic surface is unbounded, not duplicating** — only 1 flag ID ever persists verbatim (`FLAG-CR-002` v1→v2 and `FLAG-CR-013` v3→v4). Every other cycle introduces *fresh, content-distinct* concerns on new surface area: v1 attacks scaffold backward-compat (`FLAG-CR-001` "CLI signature mismatch: stop condition requires --pack/--orchestrator/--fixture flags, plan retains positional"), v3 pivots to undocumented internals (`FLAG-CR-012` "Runner skips gate_command for code steps and only calls record_dispatch_complete. That bypasses…"), v5 finds a real-but-deeper bug (`FLAG-CR-018` "Smoke orchestrator's produces path doesn't match the subprocess output filename. produces={'out': file_nonempty()} defaults the path to the produces name 'out'; subprocess writes 'out.json'…"). These are not duplicate IDs under new names — they're genuine new issues the prior plan didn't address because revise hadn't gone there yet.

2. **Revise was effective, then collapsed at v6** — gate's `signals_assessment` is explicit: *"Score trajectory 27 → 31.5 → 29.5 → 30 → 30 → 49, jumping the wrong direction at iteration 6 with the highest delta (93%) yet."* Plan word count v5→v6 dropped from 2615 to 1166 (revise *truncated* the plan rather than refining it). And `revise_v6_raw.txt` is 38 bytes of mojibake: `"Let me192.168.1.1直接运行测试。"` — the Hermes/Deepseek model essentially failed, the harness's first-attempt structural-validator caught it (`"Hermes worker returned invalid JSON for step 'revise': could not extract JSON from response (24 chars)"` in `state.json` history), the retry produced a thinned plan that *introduced fresh hallucinations*.

3. **The v6 hallucinations are the smoking gun for (E)** — `FLAG-CR-020`: *"Plan v6 narrative falsely claims 'No builtin/hype/ folder exists', contradicting actual repo state (folder present with run.py, orchestrator.yaml, etc.) and the plan's own hype.py docstring referencing the legacy folder."* `FLAG-CR-021`: *"Plan Step 1 prescribes a 'repair' for non-corrupted code. Lines 76 and 191 of author_test_runner.py are syntactically complete; the quoted truncations appear to be OCR artifacts in the plan author's view."* Last-gate rationale: *"the plan writer cannot reliably observe repo state. This is not a plan-quality issue another iteration will fix; it is a perception/verification failure mode."*

## Implication for the gate.py:218 cap-on-iteration handler fix

**The cap papers over the symptom of (B) but does not address (E), and on this run it would have helped.** Specifically:

- **Against (B) — unbounded critic surface:** The cap is the right backstop. Through v5 the loop was making real progress (addressed/open ratio improved monotonically: 0/15 → 6/12 → 9/9 → 11/7 → 14/4) but each new clean revision exposed a deeper layer of real bugs the critic hadn't yet seen. Without a cap this could plausibly run forever on a complex plan; the cap converts "unbounded but productive" into a bounded ESCALATE that a human can act on. Fine.

- **Against (E) — revise hallucination at iter 6:** The cap *masks* it. v6 produced an objectively worse plan (score jumped 30→49, body shrank by 55%, raw output was 24 chars of garbage on first attempt, retried output invented two repo-state lies). The handler-side cap at iter ≥ 6 would force ESCALATE *before* iter 6 ever ran — saving the wasted Deepseek call and avoiding the hallucinated output entering the artifact stream. So in this specific run, capping at 5 (or 6 with cap evaluated *before* revise) helps. But it's accidental: if the same hallucination had hit at iter 3, the cap wouldn't fire and we'd have a corrupt plan with no signal beyond a higher score.

- **What the cap does not solve:**
  1. **Silent revise retry-on-error:** the harness retried v4/v5/v6 first-attempt failures and accepted the second attempt without surfacing anything to the gate. In v6 the retried output was hallucinated. A real fix would treat repeated revise-validator failures as a quality signal (force ESCALATE on first revise error at iter ≥ N, or feed the validator failure into the gate's `signals_assessment`).
  2. **Score-regression detection:** v6's score jumped 30→49 (worse than any prior iter). A score-delta gate ("if score worsens by >X%, ESCALATE regardless of iteration") would catch (E) at any iteration, not just at the cap. The gate's own rationale already computed this delta — it just didn't trigger on it.
  3. **Critic-explores-without-budget:** the cap bounds wall-clock waste but doesn't tell the user *why* the loop didn't converge. A smarter signal would be "addressed-rate ≥ 80% but new flags > 0 for K consecutive iters → critic-saturating-not-deadlock; ESCALATE with 'plan progress real, scope unbounded' rather than 'plan quality degraded.'"

**Recommendation:** keep the cap (it is the right backstop for B), but add (a) a revise-retry-on-error counter that promotes to ESCALATE on second occurrence, and (b) a score-regression check independent of iteration count. On this run, (a) would have caught v4 already (first revise error of the run), and (b) would have caught v6 cleanly. The cap alone leaves both (D)-adjacent silent retries and (E) regressions invisible.

61	        self,

64	    ) -> tuple[OrchestratorDefinition, ...]:

66	            validate_orchestrator_definition(orchestrator)
67	        self._validate_child_executors(executor_registry=executor_registry)
68	        self._validate_child_orchestrators()

72	        return {"orchestrators": [orchestrator.to_dict() for orchestrator in self.list(kind=kind)]}

75	        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(kind=kind), indent=indent, sort_keys=True)

77	    def as_mapping(self) -> MappingProxyType[str, OrchestratorDefinition]:
78	        return MappingProxyType(dict(self._orchestrators))

80	    def _validate_child_executors(self, *, executor_registry: ExecutorRegistry | None) -> None:
81	        registry = executor_registry or self._executor_registry or load_default_executor_registry()
82	        known_executor_ids = set(registry.as_mapping())
83	        for orchestrator in self._orchestrators.values():
84	            for child_executor in orchestrator.child_executors:
85	                if child_executor not in known_executor_ids:
86	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(
87	                        f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} references unknown child executor {child_executor!r}"
88	                    )
89	
90	    def _validate_child_orchestrators(self) -> None:
91	        known_orchestrator_ids = set(self._orchestrators)
92	        graph: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
93	        for orchestrator in self._orchestrators.values():
94	            children: list[str] = []
95	            for child_orchestrator in orchestrator.child_orchestrators:
96	                if child_orchestrator not in known_orchestrator_ids:
97	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(
98	                        f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} references unknown child orchestrator {child_orchestrator!r}"
99	                    )
100	                if child_orchestrator == orchestrator.id:
101	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} cannot reference itself")
102	                children.append(child_orchestrator)
103	            graph[orchestrator.id] = tuple(children)
104	        self._validate_no_cycles(graph)
105	
106	    def _validate_no_cycles(self, graph: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]) -> None:
107	        visiting: set[str] = set()
108	        visited: set[str] = set()
109	        stack: list[str] = []
110	
111	        def visit(orchestrator_id: str) -> None:
112	            if orchestrator_id in visited:
113	                return
114	            if orchestrator_id in visiting:
115	                cycle = stack[stack.index(orchestrator_id) :] + [orchestrator_id]
116	                raise OrchestratorRegistryError(f"orchestrator cycle detected: {' -> '.join(cycle)}")
117	            visiting.add(orchestrator_id)
118	            stack.append(orchestrator_id)
119	            for child in graph.get(orchestrator_id, ()):
120	                visit(child)
121	            stack.pop()
122	            visiting.remove(orchestrator_id)
123	            visited.add(orchestrator_id)
124	
125	        for orchestrator_id in sorted(graph):
126	            visit(orchestrator_id)

32	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
33	        return {
34	            "id": self.id,
35	            "name": self.name,
36	            "version": self.version,
37	            "root": str(self.root),
38	            "manifest_path": str(self.manifest_path),
39	            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
40	        }
